title: Coconut rolls, banana bread and rock buns from a small oven
course_title: Basic Baking & Snacks Production: Hands-On Small Batches for Sale

say: Coconut rolls, banana bread and rock buns from a small oven.
This is the video for module 3 of Basic Baking and Snacks Production.

Coconut bread uses cheap local coconut and sells well by the piece. Blend grated coconut with warm water and squeeze out about 300 ml of milk. Fresh coconut milk spoils quickly, so use it within a few hours.

say: Mix the dough and knead it for 10 to 12 minutes. Stretch a small piece: if it goes thin enough to let light through without tearing, it is ready. That is the windowpane test.

say: To make more, do not guess. For example, Efe in Warri has an order for 30 rolls of 80 g. That is 2,400 g of dough.

panel.heading: Scaling up for 30 rolls
items: Dough needed: 30 x 80 g = 2,400 g
Factor: 2,400 / 995 = 2.41, round to 2.5
Makes 31 rolls: one spare to check

say: The recipe makes 995 g. 2,400 divided by 995 is 2.41, and she rounds up a little to 2.5, to cover dough that sticks to the bowl.

say: Black-speckled bananas are cheap and perfect: the riper, the sweeter. Reject any with mould or a fermented smell. Weigh the peeled banana, because counting gives uneven loaves.

Bake 50 to 60 minutes; skewer comes out clean

say: Pour the wet into the dry and fold only until no dry flour shows. Small lumps are fine. Over-mixing gives a tough loaf full of tunnels.

say: A whole loaf needs less wrapping and keeps longer uncut.

panel.heading: Sell whole or by the slice?

say: Slices often earn more per loaf. For example, Yetunde in Abeokuta supplies a cafe with 30 slices every Friday: three loaves of 10 slices. Cool completely, slice evenly and wrap each one. If you add nuts, say so on the label.

panel.heading: Sell whole or by the slice?

say: For rock buns, rub cold margarine into the flour and make a stiff dough. Put rough heaps on the tray and do not smooth them. Warm margarine or a wet dough makes them spread flat.

For coconut candy, dissolve sugar in water, then stop stirring and let it boil. At light amber, add the coconut, stir, and scoop small pieces with two spoons. For example, Grace in Calabar makes both from one coconut: 42 items for her stall.
Cooking sugar gets far hotter than boiling water, and it sticks to skin. Wear long sleeves, use a long-handled spoon, and keep children out.

cards.d: Long sleeves, long-handled spoon, children out of the kitchen.
Never taste from the pot. Never touch the mixture until it has cooled.
Cool under running water for 20 minutes. No butter, oil or toothpaste. Do not peel off sugar.

say: Never taste from the pot, and never use your fingers to shape it.

cards.d: Long sleeves, long-handled spoon, children out of the kitchen.

Cool under running water for 20 minutes. No butter, oil or toothpaste. Do not peel off sugar.

say: If hot sugar touches skin, cool it under cool running water for 20 minutes. Do not peel off stuck sugar, and do not put butter, oil, toothpaste or raw egg on a burn. Get medical help for large burns.

say: To remember. Knead to the windowpane test and divide by weight. Scale by total dough weight. Fold banana batter gently. Cool everything before bagging. And treat hot sugar with great care. Fresh coconut shortens shelf life, so sell quickly.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Windowpane test, then divide dough by weight
Scale by total dough weight, rounded up
Fold banana batter only until combined
Cool completely before bagging or slicing
Hot sugar: sleeves, spoons, never fingers

say: Now practise. Bake a batch of coconut rolls and work out the quantities for 45. Bake and slice a banana loaf and keep a 4-day log. Then make rock buns and coconut candy from one coconut.
